Author: Rajiv Gupta

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 65
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 25156 of 2021

Applicant :- Piyush Rastogi And 2 Others
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Kumar,Amit Misra

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Santosh Kumar Mishra,Suneel
Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
Sri Sandeep Kumar Dubey, Advocate has filed vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party No. 2 today
in Court, which is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State, Sandeep Kumar Debey, learned counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to quash the charge sheet as well as entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 722 of 2021 (State vs. Piyush Rastogi and others)
arising out of Case Crime No. 0727 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 313, 504 IPC and 3/4 of D.P. Act,
P.S. Subhash Nagar, District- Bareilly, pending in the court of F.T.C. Civil, Bareilly.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party No. 2 is the wife of applicant No. 1 and applicant Nos. 2 and 3 are her mother in-law and brother in-law.
Learned counsel for the applicant has next submitted that on account of matrimonial discord, the present criminal case was instituted against the applicants.

This Court vide order dated 20.12.2021 had directed the parties to appear before Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court, Allahabad in order to enable the parties to reach an amicable settlement.

entities.text: Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court, Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Pursuant to the said order, the applicant No. 1 and opposite party No. 2 appeared before the mediation centre and with the help of the mediator, the dispute has finally been settled between the parties and a settlement-agreement dated 21.10.2022 has been drawn, a copy of which has been annexed with the record of this application, which shall form part of this application.

Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that as per the settlement-agreement, both the parties are re-united and are living together as husband and wife and leading a happy married life.
Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the compromise made between the parties, the entire proceedings be quashed.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has also appeared and has acknowledged the said agreement and reiterated the same fact that the parties have re-united and are living together as husband and wife and leading a happy married life and, on instruction, has stated that she has no objection if the same is quashed.

This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of :-
1. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
2. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].
3. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others ( 2008) 16 SCC 1.
4. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303.
5. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab ( 2014) 6 SCC 466.
Wherein the Apex Court has categorically held that compromise can be made between the parties even in respect of certain cognizable and non compoundable offences.

sentences.text: This application under Section 482 CrPC is accordingly allowed.
It is further noted that at the time of referring the said matter to the Mediation and Conciliation Centre, High Court, Allahabad, the applicants was directed to pay a sum of Rs. 50,000/-.

The applicants had already deposited a sum of Rs. 50,000/- through demand draft No. 362277 dated 24.12.2021 at the Mediation Centre, however the opposite party No. 2 has not been paid any amount out of the said amount of Rs. 50,000/-.
In view of the above, let opposite party No. 2 be made payment of Rs. 45,000/- through demand draft by keeping Rs. 5000/- as mediation expenses within a month from the date of this order.
